newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol retail share price seen about 6,100 ptas.
newsitem.headline: Repsol retail share price seen about 6,100 ptas.

text.p: The Spanish public will pay roughly 6,100 pesetas per Repsol share in this month's privatisation, well beneath the maximum possible price of 6,327 pesetas for the share offer, analysts said on Tuesday.

Under the rules of the privatisation, the retail price will be based on the least expensive of three options -- which is likely to be a four percent discount on next Monday's average price, analysts said.
The ceiling is not likely to be touched because the share is not seen rising further in coming days, but rather trading sideways, analysts said.

"Normally the definitive price is always less than the maximum set for the offer, although if the market is very bullish it's possible that it's not far off in the end," said Patricia Fernandez, analyst at Benito y Monjardin brokerage.

The offer prospectus states that the final sale price for the retail tranche will be the lowest of three: the average traded price on Monday 28 April with a discount of four percent, the maximum set by state holding company Sepi yesterday of 6,327 pesetas and the institutional price.

Dealers predict that share indices are likely to consolidate recent heavy gains in the next week, and Repsol should move in line with the market, or may even underperform, suggesting that the actual price will undershoot the ceiling price of 6,327.

"The maximum retail price may serve as a reference for the institutional placement, where I see a range of between 6,300-6,400 pesetas, while for the small shareholder the price will be around 6,100 pesetas", said Josep Prats, of Ahorro Corporacion Financiera brokerage.
At 1250 GMT, Repsol was up 0.31 percent to 6,390 while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was down 0.13 percent to 5,663.72.
The government is selling its last 10.0 percent stake in the energy group to convert Repsol into a fully privatised entity by April 29.
Of the initial 22.95 million share offering, 12.75 million are being offered to the Spanish public who have until Thursday to make their provisional subscriptions firm.
The retail tranche was 37 times oversubscribed after the provisional period closed on Monday, Sepi said.
This strong demand led analysts to predict that the number of shares on offer to the public would be increased, with the institutional tranche losing out.
Sources close to Sepi said an increase in the retail tranche may be announced this weekend, although analysts said the demand for shares was exaggerated by the design of the offer.
Lead managers provide would-be shareholders with an estimate of how many shares they are likely to be allocated when they make a provisional order.
"People know what the trick is and if they want 500,000 pesetas worth of shares, they request 10 million so that as many as possible can be given to them," said one analyst.

According to the requests for shares made, the approximate pro rata allocation would give every 50,000 pesetas bid around seven shares, and a 10 million peseta bid would receive 30 shares in the final event, Sepi said on Monday.
Although the demand was not fully credible, it was clear that there is a big appetite for privatisations, a factor which will help the sale of electricity giant Endesa this autumn.
"Recent placements show a great reception by private investors, and this could mean the state sells around 33 percent of Endesa," B&M's Fernandez said.
